summary: TechCrunch's Anna Heim asked eight authors with ties to the startup community to each recommend one book to give as a gift this holiday season, after briefly introducing each author's own book. Picks range from science fiction and privacy history to leadership, data history, product marketing, product design and technology policy. The article notes that responses were lightly edited and that affiliate links may earn TechCrunch a commission.
one_line: Eight startup-community authors each recommend one gift book for the 2023 holidays, spanning fiction, tech history, leadership, marketing and product design.
key_facts: Jon Evans, a former TechCrunch columnist and CTO, wrote the novel "Exadelic", his first novel in over a decade, set in Silicon Valley where a tech exec is threatened by a rogue AI; he recommends "The Steerswoman" by Rosemary Kirstein.
Jon Evans says The Steerswoman series looks like clichéd fantasy but is actually meticulously thought-out science fiction and a meditation on science and how knowledge is hoarded rather than shared.

Kashmir Hill wrote "Your Face Belong to Us" about Clearview AI, a small AI company that gave facial recognition to law enforcement, billionaires and businesses; she recommends "The Listeners: A History of Wiretapping in the United States" by Brian Hochman, a Georgetown professor of American Studies.

Jerry Neumann, a veteran VC, co-wrote "Founder vs Investor" with entrepreneur Elizabeth Zalman; he recommends "How Data Happened: A History from the Age of Reason to the Age of Algorithms" by Chris Wiggins and Matthew L. Jones, both Columbia professors.

Barr Moses, CEO and co-founder of data observability startup Monte Carlo, co-wrote O'Reilly's "Data Quality Fundamentals"; she recommends Brené Brown's "Dare to Lead", published in 2018, which distills four key skill sets of great leaders.

Polina Marinova Pompliano's newsletter The Profile led to her first book "Hidden Genius"; she recommends Lynsey Addario's war photojournalism memoir "It's What I Do: A Photographer's Life of Love and War".

Georgiana (Gia) Laudi runs the agency Forget the Funnel and co-wrote the book of the same name with Claire Suellentrop; she recommends "Loved: How to Rethink Marketing for Tech Products" by Martina Lauchengco.
Laudi notes that Loved introduces four fundamentals of product marketing, the first and most critical being customer insight.

Scott Hurff, author of "Designing Products People Love", recommends "Getting Real" (2006) by Jason Fried, David Heinemeier Hansson and Matthew Linderman, based on how 37signals shipped Basecamp, which launched in 2004.

James Wise, a London-based partner at Balderton Capital, wrote "Start-up Century", launched in the U.K. on November 23; the excerpt shows his pick as "The Coming Wave" by Mustafa Suleyman with Michael Bhaskar.
The article was written by Anna Heim and published by TechCrunch on December 1, 2023.
